lessons.problem: Clicking 'Edit Work' on SongDetailPage caused a 1–3 second UI freeze. The CreativeDrawer (1408 lines, multiple tRPC queries) was statically imported and mounted synchronously on the already-heavy SongDetailPage.
lessons.solution: Replaced static import with React.lazy() to code-split the CreativeDrawer into its own 78KB chunk. Wrapped setEditingSong() in startTransition() so React yields to the browser during mount. Added Suspense boundary with a gold spinner fallback.

lessons.problem: No prefers-reduced-motion support. All canvas animations, constellation effects, and CSS transitions fired for users who had explicitly requested stillness. Accessibility violation.
lessons.solution: Added global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule to index.css collapsing all transitions to 0.01ms. Created useReducedMotion() hook for JS-based animations. Wired hook into constellation switch canvas and harmonic-resonance animation.

lessons.problem: Custom buttons in PlayerBar, WorkListRow, and SupportCreatorDrawer had no keyboard focus ring. Keyboard navigation was broken for the entire player. Mouse/touch users never noticed but keyboard users were completely blocked.
lessons.solution: Added global focus-visible rule to index.css: gold (#C49A28) outline with 2px offset on all :focus-visible elements. Suppressed for mouse/touch via :focus:not(:focus-visible). Added aria-label to all WorkListRow action buttons.

lessons.problem: VerifyPage — the highest-intent screen (QR scan destination) — had zero creator information, zero support action, and zero link to the creator's profile. The page proved the work existed but said nothing about the person who made it. Violated doctrine questions: attribution, support, discoverability.
lessons.solution: Added CreatorPanel component to VerifyPage: avatar with gold border, creator name, handle, bio/origin statement, work origin story in gold pull quote, Support Creator button (opens SupportCreatorDrawer), View Profile link. Extended getSongByWitnessId to return bio, originStatement, stripeAccountStatus.

lessons.problem: CreatorProfilePage had a 'Send a Gift' button that only opened a tip amount input. No way to access monthly patronage, licensing, or follow from the profile header. Supporting a creator required navigating to individual works.
lessons.solution: Replaced 'Send a Gift' with 'Support Creator' button on both desktop and mobile profile headers. Button opens SupportCreatorDrawer with all 6 options: one-time support, monthly patronage, purchase, license, follow, view provenance.

lessons.problem: Feed/social language detected in multiple places: 'Activity Feed' in DashboardPage, 'Unsubscribed from creator feed' in CreatorProfilePage. These phrases position Living Nexus as a social media platform rather than a registry and archive.
lessons.solution: Replaced all feed/social language with cathedral doctrine language: 'Activity Feed' → 'Witness Activity', 'creator feed' → 'witness subscription'. Added DesignDriftScanner to detect future language drift automatically.

lessons.problem: CathedralDivider section headers used font-serif (generic) and text-2xl (Tailwind default) instead of the cathedral type system. The most prominent visual element on the Explore page was not using Cinzel or Cormorant Garamond.
lessons.solution: Updated CathedralDivider to use font-heading (Cinzel) for section title and font-editorial (Cormorant Garamond) for subtitle. Added global semantic type classes to index.css: .ln-page-title, .ln-section-header, .ln-body-copy, .ln-caption, .ln-overline, .ln-mono.

lessons.problem: WorkListRow action buttons (Save, Add to Collection, Support) used opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 — completely invisible to keyboard users and screen readers. Touch users on mobile never saw them because hover doesn't exist on touch.
lessons.solution: Changed to sm:opacity-0 sm:group-hover:opacity-100 — always visible on mobile (no hover), hover-reveal only on desktop (sm: breakpoint). Added aria-label to all three buttons.

lessons.problem: The Edit Work button on SongDetailPage caused a UI freeze because the CreativeDrawer was synchronously imported and mounted. The issue was not the context split (which was correct) but the synchronous mount of a 1408-line component on an already-heavy page.
lessons.solution: Root cause: static import at the top of WorkEditorContext.tsx. Fix: React.lazy() + startTransition(). The drawer is now a separate 78KB chunk that loads asynchronously. The Suspense boundary shows a gold spinner during the first load, then the chunk is cached.

lessons.problem: Living Nexus had rich public audio and registry APIs but no native television surface. A browser-wrapper approach would have made the creator's attribution and immutable WID record difficult to navigate with a Roku remote and risked creating an independent, stale data model.
lessons.solution: Added a bounded, read-only Roku home projection from the existing public song records and a standalone SceneGraph/BrightScript package. The channel uses a Task node for HTTPS JSON loading and carries creator attribution, WID, registration time, optional testimony, and canonical verification links as immutable presentation fields.

lessons.problem: The managed development preview was intercepted by production Open Graph middleware and returned only the static SEO body. Separately, the cinematic entry used a fixed, clipped viewport that could hide controls behind mobile browser and device chrome.
lessons.solution: Bypassed Open Graph/static-body middleware in development so preview requests reach Vite, added an idempotent React refresh bootstrap safeguard, and made the cinematic surface use dynamic viewport sizing, safe-area spacing, and internal overflow for short mobile screens.

lessons.problem: The cinematic entry delayed returning visitors because its only completion action appeared after the process phase began. Keyboard and mobile users needed a visible bypass that did not require waiting for the timed sequence.
lessons.solution: Placed an immediate, safe-area-aware Skip Intro control on the splash. It uses the existing splash completion boundary, marks the session as seen, exposes a descriptive accessible name, and leaves the full cinematic experience available through the existing entry control.

lessons.problem: Draft and Publish registration could fail with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'charCodeAt')` when an incomplete or restored tone profile supplied a missing accent string while the client assembled its harmonic signature.
lessons.solution: Centralized harmonic-signature construction in the shared Loop registration contract. The helper preserves valid deterministic accents, supplies explicit three-slot fallbacks for incomplete legacy data, and prevents malformed display metadata from blocking creator-owned Draft or Publish actions.

lessons.problem: A contextual agent workspace can accidentally become a second chat owner, a hidden persistence channel, or an authority-escalation surface when it accepts free-form Agent payloads or lets contextual state trigger playback, provenance, commerce, or diary mutations.
lessons.solution: ADR-023 Phase 1 introduced strict versioned Work/Creator/Provenance/Explore/Now Playing references, rejected extra mutation-shaped fields, labelled Agent output as a suggestion, kept state in the PNA session only, and exposed only explicit Open, Verify, and user-initiated Play actions. The Context Canvas has no query, persistence, registry mutation, commerce, or diary behavior.

lessons.problem: The existing songsRouter is a critical compatibility façade across Work registration, Registry lookup, Explore, Player telemetry, collection behavior, media, and commerce. A broad router split would risk changing public procedure contracts or weakening creator/provenance custody before the target boundaries were proven.
lessons.solution: Keeper-approved Slice 1 extracted only the read-only duplicate hash lookup into lookupExistingWorkByFileHash while retaining the identical protected songs.checkDuplicate façade, Zod input, response shape, no-match/own-match/other-creator behavior, and caller identity source. Added focused behavior, authorization, no-side-effect, full-suite, type, route-smoke, and database custody checks. The pattern is internal-helper-first with compatibility facades; it does not authorize further router separation.
